title: The UK's war on anonymity has come to America
titleZh: 英国的匿名战争已经蔓延至美国
author: slowin
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: An Effort investigation has identified a coordinated operation to influence American lawmakers by five foreign non-government organizations and their US affiliates. These NGOs have converged upon a unified strategy: use the rhetoric of ‘child safety’ to advocate for digital ID laws that would prevent adults from using the internet anonymously.

In Britain, they succeeded in passing those laws. They now form part of a system which surveils, arrests, and jails political dissidents. Digital ID laws are a key component used to strip Brits of internet anonymity, an otherwise effective technological countermeasure against authoritarianism.
British NGOs are now replicating their playbook in the United States of America, attempting to pass a patchwork of digital ID laws in 21 states and the US Congress.

One British NGO, 5Rights, registered under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, but has failed to file critical information related to its foreign leadership. All five foreign NGOs have influenced American policy, either directly or using American proxies with significant foreign management.
The Center for Countering Digital Hate (CCDH) was founded by British Labour consultants Imran Ahmed and Morgan McSweeney2.

comments.author: happymellon
comments.textRawHtml:
Perhaps I'm misunderstanding, but the war on anonymity was first (just) passed in the US at a state level as porn laws before it passed in the UK.

Are we pretending that the porn id laws weren't a first attempt at getting forums like Reddit that might "accidentally" have naked pictures liable and therefore profile everyone?

Because this is leaning on blaming to UK for everything the US is doing to itself an awful lot.
comments.textZhHtml:
也许我误解了，但针对匿名的战争首先（刚刚）在美国以色情法的形式在美国通过，然后才在英国通过。

我们是否假装色情身份法不是第一次尝试让像 Reddit 这样的论坛“意外地”对裸照负责并因此对每个人进行个人资料？

因为这倾向于将所有事情归咎于英国美国对自己做了很多事情。

children.author: mancerayder
children.textRawHtml: There are people in the replies below going back and forth about whether the US or the UK started the surveillance state first. I think as undemocratic as the US can behave in practice, it's hard not to argue that the UK won the CCTV surveillance race. London is heavily surveilled. And it doesn't help that someone just posted this: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49255496
children.textZhHtml: 下面的回复里有人来回争论到底是美国还是英国先启动了监控状态。我认为，尽管美国在实践中表现得不民主，但很难不说英国赢得了闭路电视监控竞赛。伦敦受到严密监视。 有人刚刚发布了这个，这并没有帮助： https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49255496

children.author: Blazara
children.textRawHtml: Most of the cameras in London are privately operated by residents and businesses, not the state.
children.textZhHtml: 伦敦的大多数摄像头都是由居民和企业私人运营，而不是由国家运营。

children.author: happymellon
children.textRawHtml: I'm referring to the title of the article blaming the UK for the actions of the US and US based companies.
children.textZhHtml: 我指的是文章的标题，该文章将美国和美国公司的行为归咎于英国。

children.author: RobotToaster
children.textRawHtml: Who started it isn't really important, what matters is who will kill it?
children.textZhHtml: 谁发起的并不重要，重要的是谁会杀死它？

children.author: graemep
children.textRawHtml:
I agree. The fundamental problem is moral rot in western governments in general.

I am nit saying the rest if the world is better BTW, just the problems and history have less in common.
children.textZhHtml:
我同意。根本问题是西方政府普遍的道德败坏。

顺便说一句，如果世界变得更好，我并不是说剩下的，只是问题和历史有更少的共同点。

children.author: andrepd
children.textRawHtml:
Hard not to argue in what metric? The US has Flock cameras spreading like the plague, if we're going purely based on vibes. And the Snowden disclosures about how they spy on their own citizens on a massive scale is over a decade old at this point.

Plus, a city covered in CCTV could theoretically be freer than one with much less coverage, if those cameras are recording to encrypted storage and accessible only with a judicial warrant, and the others are a lawless free for all with private and public operators hoovering up all the data.
children.textZhHtml:
很难不以什么指标来争论？如果我们纯粹依靠共鸣的话，美国的 Flock 摄像机就像瘟疫一样蔓延。斯诺登披露的有关他们如何大规模监视本国公民的信息已经有十多年了。

此外，理论上，一个被闭路电视覆盖的城市可能比覆盖范围小得多的城市更自由，如果这些摄像机记录到加密存储中并且只有在司法令的情况下才能访问，而其他城市则对所有人来说都是无法无天的自由，私人和公共运营商会收集所有数据。

children.author: ericmay
children.textRawHtml:
This doesn’t make a lot of sense to me.

First, maybe we can just eventually require Flock cameras to also record only to encrypted storage accessible by a judicial warrant. Presumably you are perfectly OK with that?

Second, privacy advocates have much to say about being surveilled at all, regardless of whether the data is encrypted or not. They’re opposed to recording at all, not recording and then the judge gets to randomly decide when to release recordings.

Finally, the UK is part of Five Eyes.
children.textZhHtml:
这对我来说没有多大意义。

首先，也许我们最终可以要求 Flock 摄像机也只能记录到司法令可访问的加密存储中。想必您对此完全同意？

其次，隐私倡导者对于受到监视有很多话要说，无论数据是否加密。他们根本反对录音，不录音，然后法官随机决定何时发布录音。

最后，英国是五眼联盟的一部分。

children.textRawHtml:
> maybe we can just eventually require Flock cameras to also record only to encrypted storage accessible by a judicial warrant

This is a private company's proprietary photography and derivative works. While counties and states might be able to insist on such stipulations as conditions of use of public right-of-way, no such requirements would be legal otherwise.

Home Depot's CCTV footage is no different than Flock's footage captured from their parking lot.
children.textZhHtml:
> 也许我们最终可以要求 Flock 摄像机也只能记录到司法令可访问的加密存储

这是一家私人公司的专有摄影和衍生作品。虽然县和州可能能够坚持使用公共通行权的条件等规定，但否则此类要求就不合法。

家得宝的闭路电视录像与弗洛克从其停车场拍摄的录像没有什么不同。

children.author: ericmay
children.textRawHtml: Sure but that's all aligned with what I wrote here.
children.textZhHtml: 当然，但这与我在这里写的内容一致。

children.author: happymellon
children.textRawHtml:
You missed out that 40% of US household have a video doorbell, 50% of which are Ring.

I find that all the metrics about CCTV very misleading, and the whole thing seems to be to distract that the article is blaming the UK for actions of the US and US based companies.
children.textZhHtml:
你错过了，40% 的美国家庭拥有视频门铃，其中 50% 是按门铃。

我发现有关 CCTV 的所有指标都非常具有误导性，整件事似乎是为了分散人们的注意力，让人们意识到这篇文章将美国和美国公司的行为归咎于英国。

children.author: xboxnolifes
children.textRawHtml: London's cctv reputation predates Snowden leaks. Though, I feel like US trying to get antianonymity laws passed started long before the UK has tried.
children.textZhHtml: 伦敦的中央电视台声誉早于斯诺登泄密事件。不过，我觉得美国早在英国尝试之前就开始尝试通过反匿名法。

children.author: pydry
children.textRawHtml: It's not really worth arguing over who is worse at violating privacy. Crucially theyre both awful, both getting worse and both treating Russia and China as an aspirational model.
children.textZhHtml: 其实并不值得争论谁在侵犯隐私方面更严重。至关重要的是，它们都很糟糕，而且都在变得更糟，而且都将俄罗斯和中国视为理想的典范。

children.author: noir_lord
children.textRawHtml:
Not to mention the UN convention on cybercrime which is a ridiculous one since it makes co-operation necessary if the penalty in the home country is 4 or more years - there are quite a few countries where speaking out against the leader, been gay or been trans will get you that (or much much worse).

Canada opposed it originally and then quietly signed it most recently, the UK didn't start this stuff though we are up to our tea drinking little necks in it as usual.
children.textZhHtml:
更不用说《联合国网络犯罪公约》了，这是一项荒谬的公约，因为如果在本国的刑罚为四年或以上，则合作是必要的 - 有相当多的国家，公开反对领导人，无论是同性恋还是变性人，都会得到这样的结果（或者更糟）。

加拿大最初反对它，然后最近悄悄签署了它，英国并没有开始这件事，尽管我们已经做好了喝茶的小脖子像往常一样在里面。

children.author: volkl48
children.textRawHtml: The US is not currently a signatory to that, just to note.
children.textZhHtml: 请注意，美国目前不是该协议的签署国。

children.author: TZubiri
children.textRawHtml:
Pointing out a law you don't like in another country as justification to ignore local laws, or to critique internation relations policy, is a terrible argument.

Some country has laws that some other country dislikes, therefore they should be able to ignore them?

I think comes down to what influence you think you have. I'm a backend developer and sys admin, when it comes to international law, I think of it in relation to hosting content in other countries or serving users in other countries. Judging the quality of laws on another country is beyond my scope, if it conflicts with my ethical constitution, I just don't provide service to that country, I don't provide service in an anonymous manner that makes it possible for users of that country to evade local law because I find the law may contain bad parts.

What I'm not sure is whether you think of your influence on the subject as a sysadmin that actually wants to provide such services, or whether you think of it as some individual posturing, like a random citizen voicing their opinion on Israel v Palestina knowing full well you have no influence.
children.textZhHtml:
指出你不喜欢另一个国家的法律作为无视当地法律或批评国际关系政策的理由，这是一个可怕的论点。

有些国家有其他国家不喜欢的法律，因此他们应该能够忽略这些法律？

我认为这取决于你认为自己有什么影响力。我是一名后端开发人员和系统管理员，当谈到国际法时，我认为它与在其他国家/地区托管内容或为其他国家/地区的用户提供服务有关。判断另一个国家的法律质量超出了我的范围，如果它与我的道德宪法相冲突，我只是不向该国家提供服务，我不会以匿名方式提供服务，这使得该国家的用户可以逃避当地法律，因为我发现法律可能包含不好的部分。

我不确定的是，您是否认为您作为真正想要提供此类服务的系统管理员对这个主题的影响，或者您是否认为这是某种个人姿态，例如随机公民对以色列诉巴勒斯坦问题表达自己的看法，但他很清楚你没有影响力。

children.author: TremendousJudge
children.textRawHtml:
>Some country has laws that some other country dislikes, therefore they should be able to ignore them?

Yeah, I think that's pretty much the definition of the right of asylum.
children.textZhHtml:
>某些国家/地区制定了其他国家/地区不喜欢的法律，因此他们应该能够忽略这些法律？

是的，我认为这几乎就是庇护权的定义。

children.author: TZubiri
children.textRawHtml:
Not sure if asylum is relevant here. Crucially, asylum is granted when the person is already on the jurisdiction of the country that grants asylum.

Granting asylum to someone on another jurisdiction and extraditing them is already problematic.

Granting asylum remotely while they stay in that jurisdiction is unheard of.

And a system admin or service provider like us mortals, don't have the authority to grant asylum.

Like we would say in Argentina, you are peeing outside the bowl.
children.textZhHtml:
不确定庇护是否与此相关。至关重要的是，当某人已经在授予庇护的国家的管辖范围内时，就会授予庇护。

向另一个管辖区的某人授予庇护并引渡他们已经是有问题的。

当他们留在该管辖区时远程授予庇护是闻所未闻的。

像我们凡人这样的系统管理员或服务提供商没有权力授予庇护。

就像我们一样比如说在阿根廷，你在碗外面撒尿。
